drivingQuestion: How does the court determine the witnesses' intent to testify?

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ: לְמִיחְזֵי אֲתִיתוּ אוֹ לְאַסְהוֹדֵי אֲתִיתוּ? אִי אָמְרִי לְאַסְהוֹדֵי אֲתוֹ, נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל – עֵדוּתָן בְּטֵלָה, אִי אָמְרִי לְמִיחְזֵי אֲתוֹ, מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ שְׁנֵי אַחִין שֶׁרָאוּ בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהָרַג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ?
segments.en: «Rava says: This» is what «we say to» the witnesses who come to the court: «Did you come to observe» the proceedings «or did you come to testify? If» the witnesses «say they came to testify,» then if «one of them is found» to be «a relative or» otherwise «disqualified, their» entire «testimony is voided. If» the witnesses «say» that «they came to observe,» in that situation, «what shall two brothers do» in a case «where they saw someone who killed a person?» It is certainly unusual for those who witnessed the murder to not even attend the court hearing.
